rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of the destruction formula here was already given in the account of ʿĀd.
rows.anchor: مر تفسيره في قصة عاد

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī supplies an omitted phrase: God rescued them from punishment and from the disgrace that clung to them that day.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: هذا معطوف على محذوف تقديره نجيناهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khizy is disgrace whose scandal becomes visible and which makes its sufferer ashamed.
rows.anchor: والخزي العيب الذي تظهر فضيحته ويستحي من مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Strong is able to do whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: أي القادر على ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mighty is unobstructed by anything and cannot be prevented from what He wills.
rows.anchor: الذي لا يمتنع عليه شيء ولا يمنع عما أراده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says God ordered Gabriel to cry out, and they died from the cry.
rows.anchor: قيل إن الله سبحانه أمر جبرائيل فصاح بهم صيحة ماتوا عندها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that God created the cry by which they died.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الله تعالى خلق تلك الصيحة التي ماتوا عندها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dwellings means their homes.
rows.anchor: { فأصبحوا في ديارهم } أي منازلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāthimīn can mean dead, fallen on their faces.
rows.anchor: أي ميتين واقعين على وجوههم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss takes jāthimīn to mean crouching on their knees.
rows.anchor: ويقال: { جاثمين } أي قاعدين على ركبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were described as entering the morning because the punishment seized them at daybreak.
rows.anchor: لأن العذاب أخذهم عند الصباح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says the cry came at night and they awoke in this condition.
rows.anchor: أتتهم الصيحة ليلا فأصبحوا على هذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs invoke the morning when speaking of a great calamity.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول عند الأمر العظيم وأسوء صباحاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They seemed never to have lived in their homes because destruction erased their traces, except for bodies that testified to their disgrace.
rows.anchor: لانقطاع آثارهم بالهلاك إلا ما بقي من أجسادهم الدالة على الخزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing declaration that Thamūd disbelieved and was banished is explained earlier in the commentary.
rows.anchor: ألا بعدا لثمود } قد سبق تفسيره

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
rows.claim: The Kufans except Abū Bakr read the word in the singular, without wāw.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر أصلاتك بغير واو على التوحيد

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the plural form with wāw.
rows.anchor: والباقون { أصلواتك } بالواو على الجمع

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: In a noncanonical reading al-Sulamī reads baʿudat Thamūd with ḍamma on the ʿayn.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة السلمي { بعدت ثمود } بضم العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿd may describe good or evil and has the verbal noun buʿd; baʿuda is restricted to evil and has the same verbal noun.
rows.anchor: أما بعد فيكون في الخير والشر ومصدره البعد وبعد في الشر خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form أبعده الله is derived from baʿuda as a curse against someone.
rows.anchor: ومنه أبعده الله فإنه منقول من بعد لأنه دعاء عليه

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī's finite verb agrees in form with the verbal noun used in the standard wording.
rows.anchor: وقراءة السلمي متفقة الفعل مع مصدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard noun can mean a curse, making أبعده الله equivalent to لعنه الله; banishment is a deprivation, so the senses converge.
rows.anchor: أن يكون البعد بمعنى اللعنة فيكون أبعده الله بمعنى لعنه الله

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poetic phrase al-rajul al-laʿīn witnesses the sense of someone banished or removed.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله: ذعرت به القطا ونفيت عنه مقام الذئب كالرجل اللعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wazn is adjusting one thing against another for lightness or heaviness by a measuring instrument; metrical poetry is adjusted by prosody.
rows.anchor: الوزن تعديل الشيء بغيره في الخفة والثقل بآلة التعديل وإذا قيل شعر موزون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawfīq means correctness, especially correctness that occurs in obedience; only God can guide to it because He alone knows its conditions without instruction.
rows.anchor: والتوفيق من الصواب إلا أنه اختص بهذا الاسم ما اتفق وقوع الصواب عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shiqāq and mushāqqa mean hostile separation to the opposing side.
rows.anchor: والشقاق والمشاقة المباعدة بالعداوة إلى جانب المباينة وشقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiqh is understanding speech according to its conveyed meaning; it also names a religious discipline based on transmitted proofs, while uṣūl al-dīn concerns rational proofs.
rows.anchor: والفقه فهم الكلام على ما تضمنه من المعنى وقد صار علما لضرب من علوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raht means a man's clan and people; its root conveys tightening, as do tarhīṭ, intensive eating, and the sturdy, enlarged burrow called rahṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: والرهط عشيرة الرجل وقومه وأصله الشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajm means throwing stones; aʿazz means stronger and harder to overcome, the opposite of humbled.
rows.anchor: والرجم الرمي بالحجارة والأعز الأقوى الأمنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To make something ẓihri is to put it behind one's back and forget it; the phrase describes disregard for a matter.
rows.anchor: والظهري جعل الشيء وراء الظهر حتى ينساه

rows.speaker: تميم بن قيس
rows.claim: Tamīm ibn Qays's verse uses bi-ẓahr to mean leaving a request disregarded or unanswered.
rows.anchor: تميم بن قيس لا تكونن حاجتي بظهر فلا يعيا علي جوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An-nasb in أو أن نفعل means ‘or [does it command] that we do’; it coordinates with ما يعبد آباؤنا, not أن نترك, which would make the sense defective.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون قوله { أن نفعل } معطوفا على قوله { أن نترك } لأن المعنى يصير فاسدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here أو has the alternative force of ‘sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn’ and the cited statement that God is nearer to either rich or poor.
rows.anchor: وأو هنا بمنزلتها في قولك جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes من interrogative and dependent on تعلمون: you will learn who receives humiliating punishment and who is the liar.
rows.anchor: أن يكون معلقا بقوله تعلمون فيكون استفهاما وتقديره فسوف تعلمون من المخزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that parse, من هو كاذب may mean ‘the one who is a liar’ and coordinate with the object pronoun in يخزيه.
rows.anchor: بمعنى الذي هو كاذب ويكون معطوفا على الهاء من يخزيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parse takes the first من as a relative pronoun and coordinates من هو كاذب with it.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون من في قوله { من يأتيه } بمعنى الذي ويكون { من هو كاذب } عطفا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun هو is inserted because Arabic normally says من قام or من القائم, not bare من قائم or من قاعد; the segment begins a poetic citation but gives no line.
rows.anchor: وأدخلوا هو في قوله { من هو كاذب } لأنهم لا يقولون من قائم ولا من قاعد

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawrī glosses Baqiyyat Allāh as God's provision.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بقية الله رزق الله عن الثوري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb is not the keeper of God's blessings who can remove them from the people; God preserves them, so they should seek their continuance through obedience.
rows.anchor: وما أنا بحافظ نعم الله تعالى عليكم أن يزيلها عنكم وإنما يحفظها الله عليكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says he is not the keeper of their deeds; God records them and will repay them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وما أنا بحافظ لأعمالكم وإنما يحفظها الله فيجازيكم عليها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading says he is not responsible for their measuring and weighing so that they give full rights; his duty is to warn them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وما أنا بحافظ عليكم كيلكم ووزنكم حتى توفوا الناس حقوقهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The people mocked Shuʿayb's appeal because he prayed often and taught that prayer restrains evil and forbids indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: لأن شعيبا ع كان كثير الصلاة وكان يقول إذا صلى إن الصلاة رادعة عن الشر

rows.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: They meant ‘does your religion command you’; prayer stands for religion because it is among its most important practices.
rows.anchor: معناه أدينك يأمرك بترك دين السلف عن الحسن وعطاء وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They spoke about Shuʿayb's prayer in mockery.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالوا ذلك على وجه الاستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask whether his prayer commands them to leave their fathers' worship or to stop doing what they wish with their wealth, including cheating and short measure.
rows.anchor: أصلاتك تأمرك بترك عبادة ما يعبد آباؤنا أو بترك فعل ما نشاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On one view the praise is sarcastic and means the opposite: foolish and astray.
rows.anchor: قيل: إنهم قالوا ذلك على وجه الهزؤ والتهكم وأرادوا به ضد ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively they meant the praise sincerely: as a patient leader among his people, he should not oppose them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم قالوا ذلك على التحقيق أي أنك أنت الحليم في قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥalīm is one who does not hasten to punish someone who deserves it; rashīd is one who guides.
rows.anchor: والحليم الذي لا يعاجل بالعقوبة مستحقها والرشيد المرشد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One gloss identifies Shuʿayb's good provision as prophethood.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن الرزق الحسن ههنا النبوة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it means God guided him to His religion and expanded his wealth, for he was wealthy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه هداني لدينه ووسع علي رزقه وكان كثير المال عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes every blessing from God as good provision.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كل نعمة من الله سبحانه فهو رزق حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted continuation asks whether, after this favor, Shuʿayb would abandon worship; the retained words indicate the ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف أي أفأعدل مع ذلك عما أنا عليه من عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb does not forbid something and then practice it himself; he chooses for them what he chooses for himself.
rows.anchor: أي لست أنهاكم عن شيء وأدخل فيه وإنما أختار لكم ما أختاره لنفسي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the construction as Shuʿayb intending to do the forbidden act in opposition to them.
rows.anchor: ما أخالفكم إليه ما أقصده بخلافكم إلى ارتكابه عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem condemns someone who forbids a trait and then does it himself, supporting Shuʿayb's claim of consistency.
rows.anchor: لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله عار عليك إذا فعلت عظيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says he does not seek to draw personal gain from what he forbids, such as keeping the profit from short measure.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه وما أريد اجترار منفعة إلى نفسي بما أنهاكم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His commands and prohibitions aim only to set right the people's religious and worldly affairs.
rows.anchor: لست أريد بما آمركم به وأنهاكم عنه إلا اصلاح أموركم في دينكم ودنياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means as much as he is able and capable.
rows.anchor: أي ما قدرت عليه وتمكنت منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His ability to obey and refrain comes only from God; it is not his own power but God's assistance, grace, and facilitation.
rows.anchor: وليس ما أفعله بحولي وقوتي بل بمعونة الله ولطفه وتيسيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawakkul is contentment with God's governance, entrusting matters to Him, and holding fast to obedience.
rows.anchor: والتوكل على الله الرضا بتدبيره مع تفويض الأمور إليه والتمسك بطاعته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets Shuʿayb's return as his return to God at the resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي وإليه أرجع في المعاد عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says he returns to God through his deeds and intention, directing all his works to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إليه أرجع بعملي ونيتي عن الحسن ومعناه أني أعمل أعمالي كلها لوجه الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj glosses the warning as ‘do not let opposition and hostility to me bring upon you’ the immediate punishment.
rows.anchor: أي لا يكسبنكم خلافي ومعاداتي { أن يصيبكم } عذاب العاجلة عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says not to let enmity toward Shuʿayb lead them to disobey their Lord and suffer punishment like earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا تحملنكم عداوتي على مخالفة ربكم فيصيبكم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hostility arose because Shuʿayb called them to leave ancestral idol worship and fulfill measures and weights, which they found burdensome.
rows.anchor: وكان سبب هذه العداوة دعاؤه لكم إلى مخالفة الآباء والأجداد في عبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier peoples were destroyed respectively by drowning, the barren wind, and the earthquake.
rows.anchor: من الهلاك بالغرق { أو قوم هود } بالريح العقيم { أو قوم صالح } بالرجفة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Lot's people are not far away in time from Shuʿayb's people.
rows.anchor: أي هم قريب منكم في الزمان الذي بينه وبينكم عن قتادة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says their town is near yours, so you should take warning from them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أن دارهم قريبة من داركم فيجب أن تتعظوا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should seek forgiveness from God and then attain it through repentance.
rows.anchor: أي اطلبوا المغفرة من الله ثم توصلوا إليها بالتوبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the first command as seeking forgiveness for the past and repentance as resolving to change in the future.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه استغفروا للماضي واعزموا في المستقبل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss is to ask forgiveness and then persist in repentance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استغفروا ثم دوموا على التوبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further gloss contrasts public asking for forgiveness with inward remorse for the past.
rows.anchor: قيل استغفروا في العلانية ثم أضمروا الندامة في القلب عن الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is merciful to His servants, accepting their repentance and pardoning their sins.
rows.anchor: فيقبل توبتهم ويعفو عن معاصيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wadūd means loving them, that is, willing their benefit.
rows.anchor: أي محب لهم ومعناه مريد لمنافعهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God shows affection to His servants through abundant beneficence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه متودد إلى عباده بكثرة إنعامه عليهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation takes Wadūd as the lover who loves them when they obey Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: { ودود } بمعنى الواد أي يودهم إذا أطاعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source reports that the Prophet called Shuʿayb the orator of the prophets; no grading or chain is given here.
rows.anchor: كان شعيب خطيب الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Literally, they say they do not understand much of what he says.
rows.anchor: أي ما نفهم عنك معنى كثير من كلامك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they mean they will neither accept nor act on much of his message, using ‘I don't know what you say’ as a refusal despite understanding him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا نقبل كثيرا منه ولا نعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They said this only after Shuʿayb had established the proof against them.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالوا ذلك بعدما ألزمهم الحجة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī interprets weak as physically frail.
rows.anchor: أي ضعيف البدن عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyān interprets weak as poor in eyesight.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ضعيف البصر عن سفيان

rows.speaker: قتادة وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Qatāda and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say Shuʿayb was blind.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعمى وكان شعيب أعمى عن قتادة وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says Ḥimyar calls a blind person weak: loss of sight weakens his capacity to act, just as ḍarīr describes someone harmed by blindness.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وحمير تسمي المكفوف ضعيفا وهذا كما قيل ضرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī rejects the blindness gloss as an explanation of ‘weak among us’: the phrase ‘among us’ makes no sense if blindness is meant, since it applies everywhere.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول ليس بسديد لأن قوله فينا يرده ألا ترى أنه لو قيل إنا لنراك { فينا } أعمى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses weak as socially low or insignificant.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ضعيفا أي مهينا عن الحسن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One theological view disallows a prophet's being blind because that would repel people.
rows.anchor: فقيل: لا يجوز لأن ذلك ينفر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The opposing view allows a prophet to be blind when it causes no repulsion, like other bodily conditions and illnesses.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يجوز أن لا يكون فيه تنفير ويكون بمنزلة سائر العلل والأمراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say that but for consideration for his clan and people they would have killed him with stones.
rows.anchor: أي لولا رحمة عشيرتك وقومك لقتلناك بالحجارة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes their threat as saying they would have insulted and cursed him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لشتمناك وسببناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not spare him because he was dear to them, but because of his clan.
rows.anchor: أي لم ندع قتلك لعزتك علينا ولكن لأجل قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the poetic phrase ‘cried out in its enclosures,’ ṣīḥa means to be driven away and destroyed.
rows.anchor: ومعنى صيح في حجراته أذهب وأهلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The people of Shuʿayb are compared especially with Thamūd because both were destroyed by a blast, with Thamūd also struck by an earthquake.
rows.anchor: قالوا وإنما شبه حالهم بحال ثمود خاصة لأنهم أهلكوا بالصيحة

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj has a noncanonical reading with fatḥa on the mīm in شديد المحال.
rows.anchor: في الشواذ قراءة الأعرج شديد المحال بفتح الميم

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abū Mujliz reads بالغدو والإيصال in a noncanonical reading.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أبي مجلز بالغدو والإيصال

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī derives maḥāl from ḥīla, giving the sense ‘strong in stratagem.’
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني المحال مفعل من الحيلة

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd notes the expressions ‘he has no ḥīla or maḥāla’; the gloss is strong in stratagem.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد يقال ما له حيلة ولا محالة فيكون تقديره شديد الحيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stratagem gloss is illustrated by God's gradual seizure of people unaware and His countering of their plot.
rows.anchor: قوله سبحانه سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God countering their plot is another supporting verse for the explanation of maḥāl.
rows.anchor:
ومكروا ومكر الله
[آل عمران: 54]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īṣāl is the verbal noun of āṣalnā, entering or reaching the time of late afternoon.
rows.anchor: والإيصال مصدر آصلنا أي دخلنا في وقت الأصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arāhu yurīhi means making something visible by revealing the object or putting someone in a state of seeing it.
rows.anchor: يقال أراه يريه إراءة وهو أن يجعله على صفة الرؤية بإظهار المرئي له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cloud is a collective plural of cloud; thus thiqāl is plural, though the singular al-thaqīl would also be valid.
rows.anchor: والسحاب جمع سحابة ولذلك قال الثقال ولو قيل الثقيل لجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣawāʿiq is the plural of ṣāʿiqa, a fire that falls from the sky.
rows.anchor: والصواعق جمع صاعقة وهي نار تسقط من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary has already explained thunder and lightning at the beginning of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: والرعد والبرق ذكرنا معناهما في أول البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here maḥāl means taking someone to task with punishment; māḥalahu means matching strength until one proves stronger.
rows.anchor: والمحال الأخذ بالعقاب ها هنا فقال ماحله مماحلة ومحالا إذا قاواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī cites an Aʿshā line describing a branch as shadīd al-miḥāl, supporting the sense of strength.
rows.anchor: د غزير الندى شديد المحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istijāba and ijāba both mean responding, but istijāba also conveys the act of requesting.
rows.anchor: والاستجابة والإجابة بمعنى غير أن في الاستجابة معنى الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line, ‘no respondent answered him then,’ illustrates istijāba as response.
rows.anchor: فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓilāl is the plural of ẓill, the covering cast by a person; ẓill ẓalīl is enduring shade, unlike fayʾ, which returns after sunlight has gone.
rows.anchor: والظلال جمع الظل وهو ستر الشخص ما بإزائه والظل الظليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āṣāl is a plural of aṣl, itself a plural of aṣīl; the term evokes the origin of night and denotes the time from ʿaṣr to sunset.
rows.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل وأصل جمع أصيل فهو جمع الجمع مأخوذ من الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āṣāʾil is also used as a plural for the late-afternoon period.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال في جمعه أصائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's poem uses aṣāʾil to mean the late-afternoon times.
rows.anchor: لعمري لأنت البيت أكرم أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear and hope are not purpose accusatives with the lightning verse because the one who fears and hopes is not the one who sees the lightning; in the prayer phrase they are purpose accusatives because caller and feeler are the same.
rows.anchor: خوفا وطمعا لا ينتصبان على الغرض لأن ما ينتصب لذلك يجب أن يكون فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense is that God frightens people by showing lightning and gives them hope through it.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ها هنا يخوفكم بما يريكم خوفا ويطمعكم طمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw in ‘while they dispute about God’ can mark a circumstantial clause: God strikes whoever He wills while they are disputing.
rows.anchor: جاز أن تكون هذه الواو والحال أي يصيب بها من يشاء في حال جدالهم في الله

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Anas and Mujāhid report that a man disputed with the Prophet, asking what his Lord was made of; God sent a thunderbolt that crushed and killed him.
rows.anchor: فأرسل الله عليه صاعقة ذهب بقحفه وهو قول أنس بن مالك ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading treats the dispute clause as a follow-up after God has completed the signs of His unity and power.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون لما تمم الله أوصاف ما يدل على توحيده وقدرته قال بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If kāf is a particle, it modifies an implied verbal noun: an answering like the answering of someone stretching his hands to water.
rows.anchor: والكاف من قوله كباسط كفيه يتعلق بصفة مصدر تقديره إلا استجابة كائنة كاستجابة باسط كفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If kāf is a noun, the estimate is ‘an answer like the answer of one who stretches his hands,’ with no pronoun in kāf.
rows.anchor: إذا كان اسما محضا فالتقدير إلا استجابة مثل استجابة باسط كفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-yablugha is attached to bāsiṭ kafayhi.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله ليبلغ فاه يتعلق بباسط كفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may mean the water does not reach his mouth, his mouth does not reach the water, or the person with outstretched hands does not obtain the water.
rows.anchor: ما الماء ببالغ فاه وقيل ما فوه ببالغ الماء وقيل ما باسط كفيه إلى الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal nouns ṭawʿan and karhan are used in the place of circumstantial expressions.
rows.anchor: وطوعا وكرها مصدران وضعا موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Prophet prayed for protection from the two men, a thunderbolt struck Arbad on a hot summer day and burned him; ʿĀmir fled, threatened the Prophet, then developed a huge swelling at his knee and died in a woman of Sulūl's house.
rows.anchor: فأرسل الله على أربد صاعقة في يوم صاح صائف فأحرقته وولى عامر هاربا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's prayer was ‘O God, protect me from the two of them by whatever means You will.’
rows.anchor: اللهم أكفنيهما بما شئت

rows.speaker: عامر
rows.claim: After fleeing, ʿĀmir threatened to fill the land with mounted troops and tether a horse at every palm tree; the Prophet replied that God would prevent it.
rows.anchor: وقال يا محمد دعوت ربك فقتل أربدا والله لأملأنها عليك خيلا جردا

rows.speaker: لبيد بن ربيعة
rows.claim: Labīd ibn Rabīʿa mourned his brother Arbad, saying lightning and thunderbolts had bereaved him of a brave horseman in battle.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك يقول لبيد بن ربيعة يرثي أخاه أربدا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī glosses شديد المحال as strong in taking people to task.
rows.anchor: أي شديد الأخذ عن علي

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatāda and Mujāhid gloss it as strong in power.
rows.anchor: وقيل شديد القوة عن قتادة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses it as severe in vengeance.
rows.anchor: وقيل شديد النقمة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets it as severe in power and punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل شديد القدرة والعذاب عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says it means powerful in stratagem against unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل شديد الكيد للكفار عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: One explanation identifies the true invocation as the declaration of divine unity, ‘There is no god but God.’
rows.anchor: أنها كلمة الإخلاص شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله عن ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reasons that God is the Real, so calling on Him is the true invocation and whoever calls Him calls the Real.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى هو الحق فدعاؤه دعوة الحق ومن دعاه دعا الحق عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī takes it as the invocation by which God is called upon in exclusive monotheism; God answers the sincere caller.
rows.anchor: أنها الدعوة التي يدعى بها الله على إخلاص التوحيد عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked beside God are the idols and other beings whom polytheists call on to meet their needs.
rows.anchor: أي والذين يدعوهم المشركون من دون الله لحاجاتهم من الأوثان وغيرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The image compares idol worshippers hoping for benefit to someone reaching toward distant water that cannot reach his mouth; idols bring no benefit and answer no prayer.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله لكل من عبد غير الله ودعاه رجاء أن ينفعه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid pictures someone calling to water with his tongue and gesturing with his hand, but the water does not come.
rows.anchor: وقيل كباسط كفيه إلى الماء أي كالذي يدعو الماء بلسانه ويشير إليه بيده فلا يأتيه الماء عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan pictures someone reaching for water who dies before it can reach his mouth.
rows.anchor: وقيل كالذي يبسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فمات قبل أن يبلغ الماء فاه عن الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والبلخي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: The Arabs use ‘like one grasping water’ for striving after something unattainable.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه تمثيل العرب لمن يسعى فيما لا يدركه فيقول هو كالقابض على الماء

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An anonymous poet compares lost affection to someone holding water in his hand.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
فأصبحت مما كان بيني وبينها

rows.speaker: الشاعر الآخر
rows.claim: A second anonymous poem compares longing to water that the fingers cannot retain.
rows.anchor:
وقال الآخر:
فإني وإياكم وشوقا إليكم

words: وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers' invocation of idols leads away from truth and right guidance.
rows.anchor: أي ليس دعاؤهم الأصنام من دون الله إلا في ذهاب عن الحق والصواب

words: وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says their invocation strays from the path of response and benefit.
rows.anchor: وقيل في ضلال عن طريق الإجابة والنفع

words: ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who prostrate to God are the angels and all morally responsible creatures.
rows.anchor: { ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض } يعني الملائكة وسائر المكلفين

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Believers prostrate willingly, whereas unbelievers are compelled to prostrate at swordpoint.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن معناه أنه يجب السجود لله تعالى إلا أن المؤمن يسجد له طوعا والكافر يسجد له كرها بالسيف

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Another view says the verse means submission: believers submit willingly, while unbelievers are forced by pain and illness and cannot avoid submission to God.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن المعنى ولله يخضع من في السماوات والأرض إلا أن المؤمن يخضع له طوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their shadows also prostrate; on one view the shadow means the person, whose shadow accompanies him in prostration.
rows.anchor: قيل إن المراد بالظل الشخص فإن من يسجد يسجد ظله معه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says an unbeliever's shadow prostrates though the unbeliever does not; in precise terms the body submits but the heart does not intend worship of God, prostrating from fear.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن يسجد ظل الكافر ولا يسجد الكافر ومعناه عند أهل التحقيق أنه يسجد شخصه دون قلبه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On the literal reading, shadows' prostration is their swaying from side to side and submission through being lengthened or shortened by God's command.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الظلال على ظاهرها والمعنى في سجودها تمايلها من جانب إلى جانب

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر
rows.claim: The Kufans except Abū Bakr read يوقدون with yāʾ, in the third person.
rows.anchor: القراءة: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر يوقدون بالياء

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use tāʾ, addressing ‘you ignite.’
rows.anchor: القراءة: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر يوقدون بالياء والباقون بالتاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the tāʾ reading from the preceding address in ‘Have you then taken?’; it may also address all people generally.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي من قرأ بالتاء فلما قبله من الخطاب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading follows the earlier third-person mention of those who set up partners; it can also mean all people, as ‘what benefits people’ is general.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالياء فلأن ذكر الغيبة قد تقدم في قوله أم جعلوا لله شركاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Fī al-nār modifies yuqidūn: one can kindle upon something not itself inside a fire, as in the command to kindle clay.
rows.anchor: فجعل الظرف متعلقا بيوقدون لأنه قد يوقد على ما ليس في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wādī is the low ground at the base of a great mountain where rainwater gathers; diya is derived from the accumulation of substantial wealth paid for a slain person.
rows.anchor: الوادي سفح الجبل العظيم المنخفض الذي يجتمع فيه ماء المطر ومنه اشتقاق الدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadr is a proportionate relation without addition or reduction; wazn permits increase or decrease, and equality is qadr.
rows.anchor: والقدر اقتران الشيء بغيره من غير زيادة ولا نقصان والوزن يزيد وينقص

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads bi-qadrihā with sukūn on the dāl; both vocalizations are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بقدرها بسكون الدال وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadr can be used in either vocalization, as in expressions for a span's measure; people also discuss destiny using both forms.
rows.anchor: يقال أعطى قدر شبر وقدر شبر والمصدر بالتخفيف لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem's use of al-qadar in its line about calamities witnesses the word's form.
rows.anchor:
قال:
ألا يا لقوم للنوائب والقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥtimāl means lifting something on one's back with the bearer's strength; iḥtamalahu also describes a loud voice that someone bears without anger.
rows.anchor: والاحتمال رفع الشيء على الظهر بقوة الحامل له ويقال علا صوته على فلان فاحتمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabad is the scum of boiling, including foam on a pot or flood.
rows.anchor: والزبد وضر الغليان وهو خبث الغليان ومنه زبد القدر وزبد السيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jufāʾ is long like ghuthāʾ and originally has hamza; the verbs describe a valley producing foam and a pot shedding it.
rows.anchor: والجفاء ممدود مثل الغثاء وأصله الهمز يقال جفا الوادي جفاء

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd says jafaʾtu a man means I knocked him down, and ajfaʾtu the pot with its foam means I removed the foam.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد يقال جفأت الرجل إذا صرعته وأجفأت القدر بزبدها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says things that collect together commonly take the pattern fiʿāl, such as debris, cotton, ghuthāʾ, and jufāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء كل شيء ينضم بعضه إلى بعض فإنه يجيء على فعال مثل الحطام والقماش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īqād is putting firewood on a fire; related forms istawqada, ittaqada, and tawaqqada are also used for kindling or burning.
rows.anchor: والإيقاد إلقاء الحطب في النار واستوقدت النار واتقدت وتوقدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means something used for enjoyment or benefit.
rows.anchor: والمتاع ما تمتعت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makth is remaining somewhere as time passes; makatha, mukitha, and tamakkatha all mean to stay.
rows.anchor: والمكث الكون في المكان على مرور الزمان يقال مكث ومكث وتمكث أي تلبث

rows.speaker: جامع العلوم البصير
rows.claim: The phrase fī al-nār is an implied circumstantial modifier of the pronoun in ʿalayhi; the sense is that the material is in the fire while being heated for adornment.
rows.anchor: قال جامع العلوم البصير قوله في النار متعلق بمحذوف في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: جامع العلوم البصير
rows.claim: Ibtighāʾ ḥilya is a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial clause for the subject of yuqīdūn, meaning they seek adornment.
rows.anchor: ابتغاء حلية أي مبتغين حلية فهو مصدر في موضع الحال من الضمير

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī's analysis is that fī al-nār is not governed directly by yuqīdūn; the gold is heated while it is in the fire.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون قوله في النار من صلة يوقدون لأن المعنى ليس على ذلك

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh treats zabad as the subject, mithl as its adjective, and مما توقدون as its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقوله زبد مبتدأ ومثله نعت له والظرف الذي هو قوله مما توقدون خبره على قول سيبويه

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash instead treats the phrase as raised by the adverbial expression.
rows.anchor: وهو مرتفع بالظرف على قول الأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jufāʾ is accusative as a circumstantial expression, describing the state in which the foam goes away.
rows.anchor: وموضع جفاء نصب على الحال أي يذهب على هذه الحالة قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives two illustrations of truth and falsehood: water with foam, and precious metals or other materials heated in fire with their slag.
rows.anchor: ثم ضرب سبحانه مثلين للحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain.
rows.anchor: { أنزل من السماء ماء } أي مطرا

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والجبائي
rows.claim: The streams carry water in proportion to their size: a small stream to its smallness and a large one to its largeness.
rows.anchor: والكبير على قدر كبره فسالت كل نهر بقدره عن الحسن وقتادة والجبائي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the streams receive the amount of water apportioned to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل بقدرها بما قدر لها من مائها عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foam floats high above the water; pure useful water represents truth and Islam, while transient foam represents falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي طافيا عاليا فوق الماء شبه سبحانه الحق والإسلام بالماء الصافي النافع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another model makes Qur'an the descending water, with hearts taking their share of certainty and doubt according to capacity; water is certainty and foam is doubt.
rows.anchor: فالماء مثل اليقين والزبد مثل الشك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second example concerns gold, silver, lead, and other materials melted in fire.
rows.anchor: { ومما يوقدون عليه في النار } وهو الذهب والفضة والرصاص وغيره مما يذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adornment means ornaments made from gold and silver; useful goods include things made from minerals, such as vessels.
rows.anchor: أي طلب زينة يتخذ منه كالذهب والفضة { أو متاع }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heated materials also produce foam: their slag is impurity separated from the pure substance.
rows.anchor: ليتميز الخالص من الخبيث لها أيضا زبد وهو خبثها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To strike a parable is to circulate it through lands until people use it as a familiar example.
rows.anchor: أي مثل الحق والباطل وضرب المثل تسييره في البلاد حتى يتمثل به في الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foam goes away as useless scattered matter.
rows.anchor: أي باطلا متفرقا بحيث لا ينتفع به

words: وأما ما ينفع الناس فيمكث في الأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What benefits people is pure water and useful substances; it remains in the earth and people benefit from it.
rows.anchor: وهو الماء الصافي والأعيان التي ينتفع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer and his conviction resemble life-giving water and useful gold, silver, and other substances; the unbeliever and disbelief resemble foam, slag, and metallic dross.
rows.anchor: فمثل المؤمن واعتقاده كمثل هذا الماء المنتفع به في نبات الأرض وحياة كل شيء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives these examples to people concerning their religion.
rows.anchor: للناس في أمر دينهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda counts three parables in one: Qur'an is rainwater and hearts are riverbeds, each taking an amount according to receptivity; reflection yields a great share and general assent a smaller one.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هذه ثلاثة أمثال ضربها الله تعالى في مثل واحد شبه نزول القرآن بالماء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda's second parable compares passing thoughts and Satan's whispers to foam above water: doubts arise from the soul, not from truth, and disappear while truth remains.
rows.anchor: فهذا مثل شبه الخطرات ووساوس الشيطان بالزبد يعلو على الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third illustration makes disbelief useless dross and faith pure, beneficial water.
rows.anchor: فالكفر مثل هذا الخبث الذي لا ينتفع به والإيمان مثل الماء الصافي

rows.speaker: الحسن والبلخي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Balkhī take the parable phrase as the end of the preceding passage, then begin a new sentence with ‘For those who respond to their Lord.’
rows.anchor: وتم الكلام عند قوله يضرب الله الأمثال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view connects this phrase to the prior parable: those who remain are the responders, and those who vanish as foam do not respond.
rows.anchor: وقيل بل يتصل بما قبله لأن معناه أن الذي يبقى مثل الذين استجابوا لربهم

rows.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
rows.claim: Those who respond to God's call, believe, and obey receive al-ḥusnā, Paradise.
rows.anchor: والمراد به للذين استجابوا دعوة الله وآمنوا به وأطاعوه الحسنى وهي الجنة عن الحسن والجبائي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim glosses al-ḥusnā as a good quality or condition, also describing reward and Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه الخصلة الحسنى والحالة الحسنى وهي صفة الثواب والجنة أيضا عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do not respond to God are those who do not believe in Him.
rows.anchor: أي لله فلم يؤمنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if they owned all the earth and as much again, their offer as ransom from punishment would not be accepted.
rows.anchor: أي جعلوا ذلك فدية أنفسهم من العذاب لم يقبل ذلك منهم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī says bad reckoning means every sin is counted without forgiveness; the prophetic saying about whoever is closely examined supports this sense.
rows.anchor: أن سوء الحساب أخذهم بذنوبهم كلها من دون أن يغفر لهم شيء منها عن إبراهيم النخعي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted: ‘Whoever is closely examined in reckoning is punished.’
rows.anchor: في الحديث: " ومن نوقش الحساب عذب "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation, bad reckoning is close scrutiny and interrogation.
rows.anchor: فيكون سوء الحساب المناقشة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says unbelievers are reckoned to rebuke them, while believers are reckoned so they may rejoice in what God has prepared.
rows.anchor: هو أن يحاسبوا للتقريع والتوبيخ فإن الكافر يحاسب على هذا الوجه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says no good deed is accepted and no evil deed is forgiven; the same is reported from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: أن لا يقبل لهم حسنة ولا يغفر لهم سيئة عن الزجاج وروي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes bad reckoning as bad recompense, called reckoning because it gives each person what is due.
rows.anchor: أن سوء الحساب هو سوء الجزاء فسمي الجزاء حسابا لأن فيه إعطاء المستحق حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their final destination is Hell.
rows.anchor: أي مصيرهم إلى جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mihād is a bed prepared for someone; Hell is their evil resting place and the place they have prepared for themselves.
rows.anchor: أي وبئس ما مهدوا لأنفسهم والمهاد الفراش الذي يوطأ لصاحبه
